featured_reviews.name: Mayur
featured_reviews.review_text:
This restaurant, located near Ghatkopar bus depot on Link Road and close to the Eastern Express Highway.

Since we was traveling around we decided to give a try but it turned to disappointment. Don't fall into the trap of its appearance. At first, the photos, high review count, and name may convince you, but it's a big NO. The hotel management is not malvani. The owner was unavailable, and the staff, who were not Maharashtrian, struggled to understand some things. There was lot of negative reviews about poor service and rude behavior from staff, but we didn't experience any such issues. They were good, albeit lacking some services, like not providing a finger bowl. The place was empty, with no waiting time. Although four AC units were installed, with three of them on, it still felt hot.

Now, about the taste - we ordered multiple dishes (see pictures), but they didn't meet expectations. Except for the 'Banjara kebab' and 'tandoori lollipop', I didn't enjoy much else. The 'bombil fry' was good but overpriced. They should add two more pieces for rate they added. The 'chicken fry' dish was the worst, containing bones instead of being boneless. Avoid it at all costs. The 'manchow soup' was just okay, and the 'prawns fry' wasn't impressive either. The thalis we tried - crab, king surmai, and special chicken - were below average.

The ambiance was more than okay, but the biggest reason to avoid this place is its pricey menu. We've tried many Malvani restaurants, but this one's rates were almost 1.5 times higher, without justifying the taste.

The final verdict is to avoid it if you crave good taste, all my 6 family members were unhappy and lastly, the restaurant should focus on reducing rates.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Came across this place by chance as it is situated in a bylane not easily visible. The Google reviews made me tempted to try it and I am glad to have visited this place.

The mandeli fry was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft of the inside. The taste of the coating was excellent and the combo with the green chutney and onion was superb 👌 A must try for appetizer!

Malvani prawns gravy was excellent too. It had a balanced spice level, and the prawns size and quantity was sufficient for 2 people. A must try!

The rice bhakri we had with the prawns needs a special mention, as it was super soft and thin unlike those thick and dry bhakris very common in many places.

The prawns pulav too was good in taste, and needs to be tried with a fish gravy to enjoy the combination.

A warm and cozy place, with the ambience trying to match the cuisine they serve, this place is a must try for those looking for home-cooked, freshly prepared Maharashtrian-style seafood cuisine.

While the preparation does take some time, but it is worth the wait, as we know it is being freshly prepared.
Those unwilling to wait can call and order in advance.

Visited this place with my friends after hearing a lot about it, and it truly lived up to the expectations. We had a fantastic experience—both the food and the overall vibe were excellent.

We ordered Bombil fry as a starter, along with Prawns Thali and Surmai Thali. Every single dish was 10/10. Personally, whenever I try a new place for fish, I judge it by the taste of the Bombil fry—and this one was outstanding. It was extremely fresh, perfectly crispy, and the masala was well balanced and nicely blended.

The same quality and freshness reflected in the Surmai and Prawns thali—authentic taste and very satisfying portions.

On the owner’s suggestion, we also tried their Mutton Thali for a change, and it was surprisingly excellent. The mutton was fresh, tender, and full of flavour, which is rare to find these days.

If you’re a seafood lover, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy quality fish with great taste and vibes.

⭐ 1/5 — Absolutely Disappointing Experience | Would Never Recommend

I visited this place expecting authentic Maratha coastal flavours, but the experience was nothing short of shocking. I ordered a Surmai Tawa Fry, and to my surprise, it was completely tasteless — no spice, no salt, no flavour, nothing. It felt like eating a plain, dry piece of fish.

When I politely informed the owner and requested a return, their response was unbelievably rude. Instead of acknowledging the issue or offering a replacement, they bluntly told me:

“We can’t take it back.”

“You have to take it away.”

“We will still charge you for it.”

“We can’t offer you anything else.”

This kind of behaviour is unacceptable for any restaurant claiming to serve good food. Charging a customer for something they didn’t eat and refusing to replace a tasteless dish shows zero professionalism and zero respect.

If the owner doesn’t know how to speak to customers or handle feedback, they are in the wrong business. Food quality below average and service attitude even worse.

Highly NOT recommended.
There are many other coastal cuisine restaurants that serve better food and treat customers with basic courtesy — this one is definitely not worth your time or money.

I've been passing by the restaurant on the regular and always wanted to try it out. Honestly, I don't know why we didn't come here before. And now that we have, it's hand's down my favourite Sea food restaurant, in this part of town.

I really liked the whole vibe of the place, especially the hand painted murals on the 1st floor seating area. Comfortable seating, spacious yet cosy.

Their speciality being Mangalorean cuisine, we obviously had to try the staples! So we started with their superb Prawns Rava fry, coated and shallow fried in the most crunchy rava coating, is a must have. It was so good we ordered 3 plates! Same goes for their Prawns Koliwada fry, with delicious crispy bits of curry patta, adding an amazing punch of flavour! Both these come highly recommended by everyone.

You also must try their 'Sukkha Masala' - with any seafood of your choice. We went for their Teesria or clams. The masala has a heavy dose of fresh grated coconut, spices and well balanced flavors.

For the mains, Please do not leave without trying their Ghee Roast. It's the best I've had in Bombay. Right up there with the famous one from Nagarjuna, Bangalore.  Perfect roast masala with liberal amount of cashews in it. Best eaten with Neer Dosas. I just wish their quantity was a little more. It's just enough for one good eater.

The Prawn Gassi with Kori Roti is another Mangalorean speciality you cannot miss! Their Fish thalis are also very good and reasonable too.

The verdict: Superb food and good service are a delightful combination!

UPDATE: Visited the last two times and I'm sad to say that they lost the title for the best ghee roast. Since the chef changed, the dish is very mediocre, with maybe two-three bits  of cashews in it. :( Taste is not right too

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Malvan Tadka in Mulund offers a fairly comfortable introduction to coastal cuisine, though the overall experience leans more toward a North Indian palate than an authentically bold Malvani one. The food is decent and satisfying in parts, but if you’re expecting deeply robust, coconut-forward, fiery coastal gravies, you may find the flavours slightly toned down and more mainstream.

Over multiple visits, we’ve tried a wide range of their menu. The Surmai Fry remains one of the better choices — fresh, nicely marinated, and well cooked. The Pomfret Fry, Bangda Fry, and Bombil Fry are competently done, while the Stuffed Bombil Fry stands out as one of the more memorable dishes — flavourful and prepared with care. Seafood combinations featuring Kolambi Masala, prawn preparations, and even seasonal Crab Masala offer variety, though the gravies sometimes feel milder than traditional Malvani spice profiles.

Among the non-seafood options, the Chicken (Malvani style), Mutton preparations, Chicken Masala, Chicken Sukka, and Mutton Sukka are decent, but again lean toward a safer, more North Indian-style gravy base rather than a distinctly coastal punch. However, the Chicken Gharguti Handi was exceptionally good — homely, balanced, and far more flavourful than expected. It’s easily one of the highlights of the meal.

Accompaniments like Neer Dosa, Bhakri, and Kombdi Vade (when available) pair well with the curries, and the Solkadhi offers a refreshing coastal touch to round off the meal.

Overall, Malvan Tadka delivers average, serviceable food with a few standout dishes like the Chicken Gharguti Handi and Stuffed Bombil Fry elevating the experience. It may not fully satisfy purists seeking strong Malvani authenticity, but for those looking for a milder, more accessible version of coastal cuisine in Mulund, it does an okay job. A balanced three-star experience — pleasant, but not particularly distinctive.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Sindhudurg Family Dining to celebrate a birthday, and overall it was a mixed experience.

The restaurant is very conveniently located, especially for people coming from Mulund East railway station. The management is also supportive for small celebrations like birthdays, so that’s a plus.

However, the space is quite compact with tight seating. It can feel a bit congested, and there’s definitely room for improvement in terms of space management and comfort.

Service is another area that needs attention. There was noticeable delay in serving orders, and it seemed to be a common issue across tables, not just ours.

Coming to food:

Starters like Bombil Fry, Crab Lollipop, and Chicken Tikka Kebab were good in taste. The Crab Lollipop was the highlight.

We tried Rawas and Surmai Thalis. Surmai was fresh and tasty, while Rawas was just average. The fish curry in the thali was quite bland.

Prawns Malvani Masala and Pomfret Tawa Fry were disappointing. The prawns dish had an overpowering coconut taste, and the pomfret didn’t feel very fresh.

Chicken Sukha was flavorful and well-prepared, but Kombdi Vade didn’t feel authentic—it was more like a puri.

Surmai Tawa Fry (ordered later) was again very good.

Solkadhi was impressive and better than many nearby seafood places.

One more thing to note is the portion size—it felt a bit less for the price, so overall it came across as slightly expensive for the quantity served.

Overall, it’s a decent place for seafood with some really good dishes, but consistency, authenticity, service speed, and portion sizing need improvement.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this well-known restaurant Nisarga Restuarant, Mulund, reputed for its lip-smacking fish and chicken dishes, for a family dinner. Unfortunately, our experience did not fully meet expectations.

Ambience & Seating

The initial seating arrangement was inconvenient, as the restaurant couldn't immediately provide adjacent tables for our group of eight. We were seated at two opposite-facing tables. However, after some time, the manager arranged an adjacent setup once another family left, which was appreciated.

Service

The service left room for improvement. Our starter was served later than expected, and one of the signature dishes, fish ghassi, was unavailable. Instead, we opted for fish Malvani, which took 15-20 minutes to arrive.

Food Quality

Vegetarian Dishes: Surprisingly, the vegetarian options stole the show. The Manchow soup, spring rolls, and hara bhara kabab were flavorful and arrived promptly. The mix veg gravy and paneer 65 in the main course were well-cooked and delicious.

Non-Vegetarian Dishes: The fish Malvani was decent but lacked the wow factor expected from a restaurant known for its non-veg specialties.

Overall Experience

While the vegetarian dishes impressed, the delays, unavailability of popular items, and initial seating issues took away from the overall experience.

Rating: 3.5/5

Would recommend this place for vegetarian options but with tempered expectations for service and availability of non-veg dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Carolann D'Cunha
featured_reviews.review_text: I had visited this place for lunch on Saturday. 1stly the food tast was average. We ordered 1 tisro thali , 2 biryani , 1 chicken thali. featured_reviews.name: Ash Kechum
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered Mutton Sukka for home delivery, only received thick masala gravy and 3-4 mutton very small pieces…this would cost 500₹ and was absolutely not worth the experience. Konkan Swad Mulund
⭐4.1⭐
•Fresh Seafood💯.
•Fun Dining Experience.
•Fair Quantity and Price ratio with Good Quality food.
•Good Service
•Decent Ambiance

-🥇Chicken crispy🥇

- Solkadhi
------------In Detail-----------

••••••••••••SERVICE••••••••••••
The Service was Decent , no problems at all.

SERVICE - 7/10

••••••••••••FOOD••••••••••••••

•Starters :

2 x Masala papad
- Decent Taste, good for munching.

1 x Manchow Soup
- tasted far better as expected from a Konkani restaurant, manchow soup lovers should blindly go for it.

2 x Paya Soup
- Light, savoury with herbs and garlic , no heavy spices 🎖️MUST TRY🎖️.

1 x Squid Chilli
- This was the Hero of dinner, its crispy and not rubbery,

1 x Prawns Koliwada
- Fresh Prawns, tasted sweet , the crispy coating had the flavours and not the prawns itself.

1 x Bombil fry
- Fresh Fish with mild taste and crispy coating

1 x Chicken Crispy
- Awesome, Good Quantity and outstanding Taste.

• Main Course-

1 x Chicken masala fry[ Komdi vade]
- it tasted Decent, as Compared to my Ajji's komidi Vade💯 , this is no match.

1 x Mutton masala fry
- Good Taste, Loved it by my parents

1 x Pomfret Thali
- Overall Decent Taste, good quantity, disappointed by the Solkadhi it had.

1 x Solkadhi
- This was a great messsss, it tasted as pink coloured water,
It didn't had kokam ka khatta pan and a spice to it. As a Konkani restaurant, this messed up my mood, cuz I always have high hopes on Solkadhi from Konkani restaurants.

FOOD - 8/10

•••••••••Atmosphere•••••••••

-  Comfortable, though the AC flow is not great as near will be cold and far ones will sweat. We had seated far unknowingly abt  the AC flow

ATMOSPHERE - 5/10

OVERALL - 6/10
-------------------------------
The Ambiance can be improved by better ac control, and need to get the more authentic Konkani taste.
